note: A much longer (40-section) treatment of Williamson's Knowledge and Its Limits than the prior W1-W9 lens (S0399, batch B0010): introduces its own K-INV-01..07 invariant numbering (distinct from W1-W9), re-derives the full Kernel inside/outside/above boundary, reinterprets S_t as a projection not the knowledge itself, and proposes Q(K,P,C,t) quantifiable-properties tuple and knowledge-margin M(P,A,C). May be the same underlying source re-processed at much greater depth, or a distinct document; flagging for reconciliation rather than merging.

Extraction from Robert Brandom's Making It Explicit: Reasoning, Representing, and Discursive Commitment. Proposes commitment (not fact) as the key primitive, deontic scorekeeping, material vs formal inference, an inferential-content principle, an explicitness principle, and a Commitment Ledger derived structure. Explicitly named as filling the gap between Williamson's factive/non-reducible knowledge and a workable social-discursive layer; part of the same McGinn/Floridi/Dretske/Fagin/Gardenfors/Searle/Williamson research arc (this file places itself eighth in that sequence).

aliases: Gelfond & Kahl Knowledge Representation, Reasoning, and the Design of Intelligent Agents lens
note: Extraction from Gelfond & Kahl's knowledge-representation/ASP textbook, explicitly framed by the source as a major refinement (not just another lens) of the whole KnowledgeOS model: gives a computational/executable counterpart to answer sets as possible belief states, nonmonotonic default reasoning and retraction, dynamic-domain state-transition systems, elaboration tolerance, open/closed-world distinctions, and produces 8 new invariants (K-INV-08..15), an Epistemic Model Separation Principle, and three final boxed definitions (Knowledge, Knowledge Space, KnowledgeOS Kernel).

A governance/adjudication-process document reframing constitutional question C-15 (how retraction of knowledge is represented) via a Knowledge Space + time-indexed Projection model, and reviewing a proposed Epistemic-state + Lifecycle-state split; explicitly kept as a brainstorming hypothesis (C-15-H1) pending formal adjudication, not accepted as a ruling. Distinct track from the philosophy-book-lens research arc (McGinn/Floridi/.../Gelfond-Kahl) in this same batch -- concerns KnowledgeOS constitutional/adjudication process (HPA, Kernel v1.1, Claude Session 1/2) rather than the philosophical Knowledge Space lineage, though it reuses 'Knowledge Space' and 'Projection' terms that may or may not be the same object as knowledge-space.

aliases: Knowledge Element / Knowledge State mathematical model
note: A dedicated mathematical-formalization document (following the Gelfond & Kahl extraction) proposing a formal knowledge-element tuple e, a knowledge-state K_t, a multidimensional Knowledge Measurement Vector Q(e)/K(e) (logical support, probabilistic support, unknownness, provenance coverage, inferential strength, conflict, stability, margin, scope coverage, explanatory gain, predictive accuracy), a KS=(V,E,τ,Γ,Π) architecture, and distance/flux/depth measures between knowledge states -- explicitly proposed as research mathematics, not yet a Kernel schema, and explicitly warns against collapsing these into one KnowledgeScore scalar.
